labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p4_orthogonalite_facettes
labels.notes: prop4_orthogonalite: IsConvexPart W (= KS, K(S(n)), Projective/Convex.lean:521; the target block's 'CS' is a planner slip, and CS would only be stronger), AlphaK W m m', AlphaK (D W) p p', OrthPts m p => OrthPts m' p'. Exactly the paper. The proof goes through alphaW_iff_extend on kPrime W and the dual-cone inequality: no half-line, no prop1_coneAppui, no coneAppui. OQ-162 (a) / OQ-164 (a) do not touch it. The symmetric half needs only m' in W (AlphaK.mem_right), not the bidual; the finding is correct.

labels.label: bzdef:c3s4d4_orthogonalite_facettes
labels.notes: OrthFacettes F F' := for all m in F, m' in F', OrthPts m m'. This is the paper's definition, stated for every pair of parts, so it is more general. The remark l.1028-1029 (orthFacettes_of_exists) carries IsFacetteK W F and IsFacetteK (D W) F' and goes through Prop. 4 via FK = facetteK membership. Instance def4_instance (quarter arc, {a} and {b}) is real: a0=(1,0), b1=(0,1).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p5_orthogonalite_alpha
labels.notes: prop5_orthogonalite: four IsFacetteK, FacetteKLE W F1 F2, FacetteKLE (D W) F1' F2', OrthFacettes F1 F1' => OrthFacettes F2 F2'. Faithful. It uses the library's facette alpha (FacetteKLE) and facetteKLE_iff_forall, then Prop. 4. Convention-free.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p6_facette_duale
labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, disclosed in the docstring, SCOPE and REPORT. prop6_facetteDuale proves: D(W_a) = D(W_b) on F; for each a in F, exists unique G with IsFacetteKExt (D W) G and closure G = D(W_a); and facetteDuale W F is that G. IsFacetteKExt = IsFacetteK or (G = emptyset and noyau empty) (isFacetteKExt_iff), the convention of l.289-290, which I checked in the transcription. The refutation of the genuine-facette reading is real. W = closed quarter arc of S(1), c = s(1,1), facette of c = the open arc. W_c is the least convex part containing W and -c, and the cone on (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1) is all of R^2, so W_c = S(1). Then D(W_c) = {m in D(W) = W : m0 + m1 = 0} = emptyset (D_coneAppui_c1), and no nonempty facette has empty closure. The printed proof's 'point interieur a'' also presupposes D(W_a) nonempty. prop6_facetteDuale_of_nonempty gives the genuine-facette form exactly when D(W_a) is nonempty. Convention check: coneAppui is Def. 1 (the least convex part, ConeAppui.lean:122), not the half-line Def. 1'. The proofs use prop3_coneAppui and prop2_coneAppui through mk_mem_D_coneAppui_iff / F_coneAppui_union_zero, which are half-line-free. The a in W that Prop. 3 needs (OQ-164 (b)) is supplied by hF.subset ha. No use of prop1_coneAppui (OQ-164 (a)) or of Def. 1' (OQ-162 (a)). Instances: facetteDuale_a0 (D({a}) = {b}) and facetteDuale_vertex0 (simplex of S(n+1); for n=1 the triangle of S(2): D(vertex) = the opposite open edge, a genuine facette, orthogonal). Both are non-vacuous.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p7_facette_duale_minimale
labels.notes: prop7_facetteDuale: IsConvexPart W, IsFacetteK W F, IsFacetteK (D W) F', OrthFacettes F F' => FacetteKLE (D W) (facetteDuale W F) F'. The claim 'holds under either reading of Prop. 6' is correct. F' is nonempty and contained in D(W_a) (mem_D_coneAppui_of_orthFacettes, via Prop. 3 with a in W supplied), so D(W_a) is nonempty. facetteDuale is then the genuine facette of the alpha-least point a' (facetteDuale_eq_facetteK, uniqueness among extended facettes), and a' alpha(D W) p for p in F'. So the conclusion is the same object under both readings. The commentary l.1063-1066 is proved: orthFacettes_facetteDuale and subset_closure_facetteDuale. One remaining case is not covered (see the minor finding): F' itself taken as the extended facette emptyset. Convention-free as for Prop. 6.

findings.what: SCOPE says Prop. 7 'holds under every reading of « facette » in Prop. 6'. That is true for the reading of D(F). But if the extended reading (facette emptyset of dimension -1) is also applied to F' in Prop. 7, the case F' = emptyset (possible when the noyau of D(W) is empty) is not covered. There, <F, emptyset> = 0 holds vacuously, and FacetteKLE (D W) _ emptyset is false as defined on points. In the lifted sense on kPrime it would hold, since every B alpha-precedes O in a cone. The statement takes F' as a genuine facette (IsFacetteK), which is the natural reading of 'une facette de D(W)' in Prop. 7, so this is not Lean < paper. The disclosure just does not say it.
findings.fix: Add one SCOPE sentence: Prop. 7 is stated for genuine facettes F' (IsFacetteK); with F' = the extended facette emptyset, the relation D(F) alpha emptyset is meaningful only in the lifted sense on F(D(W)) u {O}, where it holds trivially. No change to the statement is needed.
